title: Agent Learning via Early Experience
one_liner: This paper trains agents from their own early interactions, even before reward-driven learning becomes practical.
lead: Many agents learn from expert demonstrations because direct reward-driven training is expensive or impossible in real web and tool settings. This paper studies a middle stage called early experience: let the agent act, keep the resulting future states, and learn from those states before full reward optimization becomes workable.

problem.h2: Agent training often sees only polished expert paths and misses the wider environment
paras: Expert demonstrations show what a skilled path looks like, but they do not show many of the wrong turns, recovery states, and odd page conditions that appear in real use. An agent trained only on polished paths can fail when the environment looks slightly different from the narrow examples it saw during training.

Direct reward-driven learning is also hard in many settings. Some tasks have no clean automatic score, and some tasks require very long action chains before any final signal appears. The paper asks whether there is a useful training stage between expert imitation and full reward optimization.

callout.html: Use the agent's own early interactions as supervision, because those interactions expose a broader set of environment states than expert-only data does.

panels.title: 1. Expert-only training starts narrow
panels.viz_args: The agent sees only polished successful trajectories.
panels.caption: This gives clear examples but little coverage of messy real situations.

panels.title: 2. The agent explores on its own
panels.viz_args: Clicks, tool calls, and partial plans produce many future states.
panels.caption: Some of those states are poor, but they still reveal how the environment changes after an action.

panels.title: 3. Keep the resulting states
panels.caption: The training signal comes from the observed future states, because those states show what each action actually caused.

panels.title: 4. Learn world behavior and self-correction
panels.viz_args: Train on how the environment changes and on how the agent can revise poor choices.
panels.caption: The paper uses both environment grounding and self-reflection.

panels.title: 5. Generalization improves
panels.viz_args: The agent handles unseen situations with fewer brittle failures.
panels.caption: Broader state coverage matters because the agent learns from more than one expert path.

steps.text: Let the current agent act in the environment and record what future states appear after each action.
Train the agent to connect its action choices to later page or tool states so that it gains a clearer sense of environment dynamics.
Expose the agent to its own weak choices and revised choices so that it learns how to recover from suboptimal decisions.
Combine early experience with expert data so that clean demonstrations and broader environment coverage both influence training.

steps.b: Use reward training later when possible
steps.text: Treat early experience as a bridge stage because it prepares the policy before costly reward optimization begins.

paras: The paper changes what counts as useful supervision. Instead of waiting for expert labels or final reward signals only, it uses the future states caused by the agent's own early actions.

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: state coverage before reward learning
hidden.name: how many useful environment situations the agent sees during pre-reward training
paras: The paper argues that early training quality depends on the spread of states the agent experiences, not only on whether the actions were perfect. A narrow training set may produce a polished policy that breaks when the page layout, tool result, or task order changes.

Early experience raises state coverage because the agent encounters its own mistakes and partial progress states. Those states are useful because they reveal the environment that the agent will later face at test time.

heat.caption: The darkest cells mark states that expert-only data often misses but real deployments contain frequently.

reads.html: The agent gets stronger when it sees more of the environment before reward learning starts, because later tasks are less likely to place it in a state it has never encountered.
Early experience broadens state coverage and teaches recovery behavior, which means later training starts from a policy that already understands more of the task space.

paras: Early experience can help because the next observed state is a free supervision signal. When the agent clicks a control, opens a page, or calls a tool, the resulting state shows what that action caused. Training on those cause-and-effect links gives the policy a more grounded picture of the environment.

Self-reflection matters because many failures are not random. They follow recurring weak decisions, such as opening the wrong panel or following the wrong subgoal. If the training data includes both the weak move and the later recovery, the policy can learn a correction pattern before full reward learning begins.

stages.s: Collect self-generated action and future-state pairs
Train on environment grounding from those pairs
Train on revisions from weak choices to stronger ones so that the agent learns concrete recovery patterns

math.words: Useful pre-reward learning grows when broad state coverage and good correction learning both rise, because each covers a different weakness of expert-only training.
symbols: how useful the early experience stage is for later task performance
how much of the real environment state space the agent sees during early training
how well the agent learns to recover from weak early choices

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose expert-only training covers 4 out of 10 important state types, while early experience covers 7 out of 10.
Suppose the agent learns a useful recovery pattern on 8 out of 10 common mistake cases, so correction_skill is 0.8.
Then early_learning_value under this rough view is 0.7 times 0.8, which is 0.56.
That means the early stage gives useful preparation on about 56 out of 100 important situations.
The example shows why broader state coverage matters because recovery cannot help on situations the agent never saw.

math.note: The equation is a teaching summary. The paper's main lesson is that state coverage and recovery learning support each other.

bars.h2: How the training source changes the policy

charts.title: Expert-only supervision
charts.note: Expert-only data stays narrow because it mostly shows polished successful paths.

charts.title: Expert data plus early experience
charts.note: The mixed training set lifts generalization because it adds state diversity and correction examples.

items.html: If the initial agent acts almost randomly, many collected states may be low-value clutter, so the policy spends capacity learning from poor signals.

items.b: The collected states are broad but shallow.
items.html: If the agent reaches many pages without learning what caused each transition, the data volume rises but the cause-and-effect lesson stays weak.
If the agent simply repeats its own mistaken explanation, the reflection stage can preserve a weak pattern instead of correcting it.
The method works when the early policy is strong enough to reach informative states and the training objective ties each action to the future state it created.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a web or tool-use environment where expert demonstrations exist but cover only a narrow set of task orders. Train one agent on expert data only and another on expert data plus early self-generated interaction data. Measure coverage of intermediate states, recovery success after a planted wrong move, and final task completion on held-out tasks.
The demo proves the paper's point if the early-experience agent handles more held-out situations, because it learned from a wider range of environment states before any full reward stage was needed.
demo.closing: A convincing result should include at least one recovery-heavy task where expert-only training stalls and early experience carries the agent through.
